risks.title: Attracting and retaining qualified staff
risks.summary: ADUS may face challenges in recruiting and retaining qualified employees, which could increase operating costs. In the home healthcare services sector, access to competent personnel is critical.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified early in Item 1A (strong position), moderate language 'may not be able' without maximum intensity, stable trend (standard wording), key personnel category moderately weighted in the home services sector.

risks.title: Exposure to interest rate fluctuations
risks.summary: ADUS has $124.3 million of variable-rate debt. A 100 basis point increase in interest rates would reduce net income by $1.4 million. The company has no interest rate hedging in place.
risks.score_rationale: Risk detailed in Item 7A with quantitative data (124.3 M$ in 2025 vs 223.0 M$ in 2024), factual language 'would have decreased', quantified impact (1.4 M$ or $0.08 per share), increasing trend (debt down but exposure remains), credit category heavily weighted.

risks.title: Internal controls over recent acquisitions
risks.summary: ADUS acquired two companies in 2025 (Helping Hands and Gold Horses) that were excluded from the internal control assessment. These acquisitions represent a minor portion of revenues but create a temporary control gap.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified in Item 9A (mid-position), neutral language regarding regulatory exclusions, emerging trend (two acquisitions in 2025: Helping Hands and Gold Horses), industrial category moderately weighted due to minor acquisitions (0.5% and 0.2% of revenues).

ai_positioning.summary: ADUS does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K filing. Technology references are limited to cybersecurity and risk management.
